A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IHL/FILA research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite the revised title and formatting.

before.justification: v2 reports original TDEC and TOFU experiments, component analyses, and continual-unlearning results in Appendix D.1.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and reports additional comparisons and detailed TOFU results in Appendix D.2 and Tables 2–9.

M1.justification: Section 3.4 revises the prescribed FILA initialization from row-sum weighting and inverse rescaling to square-root weighting and inverse-square-root rescaling. This is a limited correction to the written computation; the PDFs do not establish an implementation change. Removing IHL's outer max(0, ...) is mathematically equivalent for probabilities.

E1.justification: Both versions use TDEC, WikiText retention, the same nine reasoning and four dialogue datasets, Pile perplexity, TOFU's 1%/5%/10% forgetting tasks, and continual unlearning. Real-author and world-fact evaluations were already documented in v2 Appendix C.

E2.justification: TOFU comparisons expand from GA/GD and the proposed variants to include KL, DPO, NPO, GA+FILA, and GD+FILA, documented in Figure 7 and Tables 2–9. GA remains in the appendix even though GD+FILA replaces it in the main Figure 5 display.

E3.justification: Figure 4 revises the stated model from GPT-Neo-2.7B to GPT-Neo-125M; this establishes a reported setting correction, not that experiments were rerun. Table 1 adds full-parameter IHL controls. The principal learning rates, ranks, sample sizes, epoch budgets, and stopping criteria remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 extends component testing through full-parameter IHL controls in Table 1 and GA/GD-with-FILA controls on TOFU. Existing rank, target-module, and continual-unlearning analyses remain. GD+FILA's TDEC rank analysis already appeared in v2 Figure 3, so its new table rows do not establish a new ablation.

E5.justification: Both versions report five TDEC forget sets and use Kolmogorov–Smirnov p-values for TOFU forget quality. The additional p-values do not change the statistical procedure, and v3 introduces no new seed, repetition, confidence-interval, or uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: v3 adds full-parameter IHL results, additional TOFU comparator trajectories, and detailed component metrics across models, ranks, and forgetting fractions in Tables 2–9. Table 1 also revises GPT-Neo-2.7B full-parameter GD reasoning accuracy from 44.0 to 51.8. These are substantial additions to the reported evidence, not a demonstrated performance improvement between versions.

T1.justification: Section 3.4 corrects the claimed closed-form WLRA solution's weighting and inverse scaling to match its square-root-weighted objective, and fixes the relative-Fisher matrix dimensions from d×r to d×k. The core derivative calculations and Appendix A proof otherwise remain equivalent.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that IHL stabilizes unlearning and FILA accelerates LoRA-based forgetting while preserving other capabilities. The new contribution bullets and parameter-efficient title retain this substantive scope; the additional experiments broaden supporting evidence.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly explains that FILA can accelerate GA's divergent behavior, making its downstream benefit depend on the loss being optimized. Sections 3.4 and 4.3 also attribute slow IHL optimization to limitations of randomly initialized LoRA weights. The existing over-unlearning and oracle-dependent stopping limitations are retained.

D1.justification: v3 adds an implementation-repository link, specifies TOFU utility's component metrics, and documents the additional baselines' regularization and reuse of experimental hyperparameters. It removes v2's direct TDEC dataset link. Hardware and principal training hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Rafailov et al. (2024) for DPO and Zhang et al. (2024) for NPO, discussing them as alternative unlearning approaches. The broader positioning relative to GA, LoRA, and PiSSA remains substantially the same.

P1.justification: The introduction and related work receive substantial rewriting and compression, explicit contribution bullets are added, and the IHL/FILA motivation and results discussion are extensively revised. The title and affiliations also change, although the overall section sequence remains stable.

P2.justification: Figure 1 becomes a fuller method overview; Table 1 gains rows, explicit method labels, colored performance differences, and highlighting. Figures 3–5 receive revised legends or displays, and Figure 7 plus eight detailed TOFU tables are added. The document also adopts the ICLR layout.

improvement.justification: v3 addresses an important weakness in v2's predominantly GA/GD-based validation through KL/DPO/NPO comparisons and additional controls separating IHL's and FILA's effects. Detailed TOFU metrics make the forgetting–utility trade-offs substantially easier to assess, while corrected FILA algebra and an implementation link improve method documentation. Losing the direct TDEC dataset link is a limited drawback relative to these gains.
